methodology.note: Dates labeled approximate or traditional are not presented as exact chronology. Formal definitions are distinguished from earliest surviving witnesses and reform events.
methodology.test_note: C3 Historical Depth staging dataset. WIP roadmap placeholders are test-only and must be removed before production release.

events.label: Traditional primeval chronology
events.title: Noah and the flood tradition
events.summary: Genesis presents the flood and covenant with Noah as a universal judgment-and-renewal pattern.

events.label: c. 1900–1700 BC
events.title: Patriarchal age: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob
events.summary: The ancestral narratives locate Israel’s beginnings in the patriarchs and the promises made to Abraham and his descendants.

events.label: c. 19th–18th c. BC
events.title: Call and covenant of Abraham
events.summary: The Abrahamic promises of land, descendants, and blessing become foundational to Israel and New Testament covenant theology.

events.label: Traditional patriarchal period
events.title: Joseph in Egypt
events.summary: The Joseph cycle explains Israel’s movement into Egypt and develops providence, suffering, and deliverance themes.

events.label: c. 13th c. BC
events.title: Exodus and Sinai covenant
events.summary: Israel’s deliverance from Egypt and covenant at Sinai form a central biblical pattern for salvation, law, worship, and later Christian typology.

events.label: c. 13th c. BC
events.title: Law and covenant worship at Sinai
events.summary: Exodus–Leviticus present covenant law, priesthood, sacrifice, tabernacle, and holiness.

events.label: c. 13th–12th c. BC
events.title: Settlement / conquest traditions
events.summary: Joshua presents Israel taking possession of Canaan; Judges follows the pre-monarchic period.

events.label: c. 12th–11th c. BC
events.title: Period of the Judges
events.summary: Judges depicts decentralized Israel before the monarchy and recurring cycles of apostasy, oppression, repentance, and deliverance.

events.label: c. 11th c. BC
events.title: Saul and the beginning of monarchy
events.summary: Israel’s monarchy begins with Saul before the rise of David.

events.label: c. 1000 BC
events.title: Davidic kingdom and covenant
events.summary: David’s kingship and dynasty become a major foundation for later messianic expectation.

events.label: c. 10th c. BC
events.title: Solomon and the First Temple
events.summary: Solomon’s reign is associated with the Jerusalem Temple and the height of the united monarchy.

events.label: c. 930 BC
events.title: Kingdom divided: Israel and Judah
events.summary: After Solomon the monarchy divides into northern Israel and southern Judah.

events.label: 9th c. BC
events.title: Elijah confronts Baal worship
events.summary: Elijah’s ministry dramatizes covenant fidelity during the northern monarchy.

events.label: 9th c. BC
events.title: Elisha’s prophetic ministry
events.summary: Elisha continues prophetic ministry in the northern kingdom with signs, healings, and political interventions.

events.label: c. 760 BC
events.title: Amos prophesies against injustice
events.summary: Amos links covenant fidelity with justice and warns the northern kingdom of judgment.

events.label: 8th c. BC
events.title: Hosea and covenant fidelity
events.summary: Hosea uses marital covenant imagery to portray Israel’s infidelity and God’s persistent mercy.

events.label: 8th c. BC
events.title: Isaiah’s prophetic ministry
events.summary: Isaiah addresses Judah amid Assyrian pressure and becomes central to later Jewish and Christian messianic interpretation.

events.label: 722/721 BC
events.title: Fall of the Northern Kingdom
events.summary: Assyria destroys the Northern Kingdom of Israel.

events.label: 701 BC
events.title: Assyrian crisis under Hezekiah
events.summary: Jerusalem survives Sennacherib’s campaign while much of Judah is devastated.

events.label: c. 622 BC
events.title: Josiah’s reform
events.summary: The discovery of a book of the law is associated with Josiah’s major religious reform.

events.label: late 7th–early 6th c. BC
events.title: Jeremiah and the coming exile
events.summary: Jeremiah warns Judah before Jerusalem’s fall and proclaims the promise of a new covenant.

events.label: c. 593–571 BC
events.title: Ezekiel among the exiles
events.summary: Ezekiel ministers among Judean exiles and develops themes of restoration, temple, shepherd, and new heart.

events.label: 587 BC
events.title: Fall of Jerusalem and Babylonian exile
events.summary: Babylon destroys Jerusalem and Judah enters exile.

events.label: 539 BC
events.title: Cyrus conquers Babylon
events.summary: Persian conquest of Babylon creates the political setting for Judean return and restoration.

events.label: 538 BC onward
events.title: Persian period and return from exile
events.summary: Persian rule permits Judean restoration; Ezra-Nehemiah preserve major restoration traditions.

events.label: 515 BC
events.title: Second Temple completed
events.summary: The rebuilt Temple anchors the post-exilic and Second Temple period.

events.label: 515 BC
events.title: Second Temple dedicated
events.summary: The restored Temple becomes the center of Jewish worship in the Second Temple period.

events.label: 5th c. BC
events.title: Ezra and Torah-centered restoration
events.summary: Ezra is associated with post-exilic religious restoration and public reading of the law.

events.label: c. 445 BC
events.title: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem’s walls
events.summary: Nehemiah’s mission strengthens Jerusalem and accompanies covenant renewal.

events.label: 332 BC
events.title: Alexander the Great enters the Levant
events.summary: Alexander’s conquests inaugurate the Hellenistic context that shapes later Jewish history and the Greek biblical tradition.

events.label: 3rd–1st c. BC
events.title: Greek Septuagint translation develops
events.summary: Jewish Scriptures are translated into Greek over time, forming the scriptural environment widely used in early Christianity.

events.label: 175–164 BC
events.title: Antiochus IV and Maccabean crisis
events.summary: Seleucid persecution and resistance form the setting of 1–2 Maccabees.

events.label: 167 BC
events.title: Temple profanation under Antiochus IV
events.summary: Seleucid policies provoke the Maccabean revolt and crisis preserved in 1–2 Maccabees.

events.label: 166 BC
events.title: Maccabean revolt begins
events.summary: Mattathias and his sons lead resistance to Seleucid religious persecution.

events.label: 164 BC
events.title: Temple rededication
events.summary: The Maccabean restoration of Temple worship stands near the close of the Old Testament historical horizon.

events.label: 142 BC
events.title: Hasmonean independence
events.summary: Judea achieves a period of political independence under the Hasmoneans.

events.label: 63 BC
events.title: Pompey takes Jerusalem
events.summary: Roman intervention ends independent Hasmonean rule and places Judea within Rome’s sphere.

events.label: 37 BC
events.title: Herod the Great begins rule
events.summary: Herod rules Judea under Roman authority and undertakes major Temple expansion.

events.label: c. 6–4 BC
events.title: Annunciation and Incarnation
events.summary: The Gospel of Luke presents Gabriel’s annunciation to Mary and the conception of Jesus by the Holy Spirit.

events.label: c. 6–4 BC
events.title: Nativity of Jesus
events.summary: The birth of Jesus inaugurates the Gospel narratives of the Messiah’s earthly life.

events.label: c. 6–4 BC
events.title: Birth of Jesus Christ
events.summary: The Incarnation opens the climactic fulfillment of Israel’s messianic hope.

events.label: c. AD 27–30
events.title: Baptism of Jesus
events.summary: Jesus’ baptism marks the beginning of his public ministry in the Synoptic Gospels.

events.label: c. AD 27–30
events.title: Public ministry of Jesus
events.summary: Jesus proclaims the Kingdom, teaches, heals, gathers disciples, and prepares the New Covenant.

events.label: c. AD 27–30
events.title: Public ministry of Jesus
events.summary: Jesus proclaims the Kingdom, teaches, heals, gathers disciples, and prepares the Twelve.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Ascension of Christ
events.summary: Acts presents the risen Christ ascending and commissioning the apostles before Pentecost.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
events.summary: Jesus is crucified under Pontius Pilate; the Passion becomes central to apostolic proclamation.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Last Supper and institution of the Eucharist
events.summary: Jesus gives the Eucharistic memorial of the New Covenant on the eve of his Passion.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Pentecost and public mission of the Church
events.summary: The Holy Spirit descends on the disciples and Peter publicly proclaims Christ in Jerusalem.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Resurrection of Jesus
events.summary: The apostles proclaim that God raised Jesus from the dead, the foundation of Christian faith.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Passion, Resurrection and Ascension
events.summary: The Paschal Mystery stands at the center of Christian faith and apostolic preaching.

events.label: c. AD 30
events.title: Pentecost and public apostolic mission
events.summary: The Holy Spirit empowers the apostolic witness and the Church’s mission.

events.label: c. AD 30s
events.title: Martyrdom of Stephen
events.summary: Acts records Stephen as the first Christian martyr and a catalyst in the wider mission.

events.label: c. AD 30s
events.title: Conversion of Saul / Paul
events.summary: Saul encounters the risen Christ and becomes the apostle to the Gentiles.

events.label: c. AD 40s
events.title: Peter and Cornelius
events.summary: Acts portrays the Spirit’s gift to Gentiles and Peter’s role in recognizing their admission.

events.label: c. AD 40s
events.title: Disciples called Christians at Antioch
events.summary: Acts identifies Antioch as a major missionary center and the place disciples were first called Christians.

events.label: c. AD 49
events.title: Council of Jerusalem
events.summary: Apostles and elders resolve the Gentile circumcision controversy, providing a foundational model of conciliar discernment.

events.label: c. AD 49
events.title: Council of Jerusalem
events.summary: Acts 15 records an apostolic council resolving a major question concerning Gentile Christians.

events.label: AD 40s–50s
events.title: Pauline missionary journeys
events.summary: Paul and companions establish and strengthen churches across the eastern Mediterranean.

events.label: c. AD 50–51
events.title: Early Pauline letters
events.summary: 1 Thessalonians is commonly dated among the earliest surviving New Testament writings.

events.label: c. AD 57
events.title: Paul writes Romans
events.summary: Romans gives a major apostolic exposition of the Gospel, grace, faith, Israel, and Christian life.

events.label: AD 64
events.title: Neronian persecution at Rome
events.summary: After the fire of Rome, Nero’s persecution becomes an early landmark of Christian martyrdom.

events.label: c. AD 64–67
events.title: Martyrdoms of Peter and Paul
events.summary: Ancient Christian tradition locates the martyrdoms of Peter and Paul at Rome under Nero.

events.label: c. AD 64–67
events.title: Martyrdoms of Peter and Paul at Rome
events.summary: Ancient Christian tradition places the martyrdoms of Peter and Paul at Rome during Nero’s reign.
events.source: Clement of Rome; Eusebius; New Advent

events.label: c. AD 65–75
events.title: Gospel of Mark
events.summary: Mark is commonly dated around the period of the Jewish War and is often regarded as the earliest canonical Gospel.

events.label: AD 70
events.title: Jerusalem and the Temple destroyed
events.summary: Roman forces destroy Jerusalem and the Second Temple, profoundly reshaping Jewish and Christian history.

events.label: AD 70
events.title: Destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple
events.summary: Roman forces destroy Jerusalem and the Temple, reshaping Jewish and Christian history.

events.label: c. AD 80–90
events.title: Matthew and Luke-Acts
events.summary: Matthew and Luke-Acts are commonly dated to the later first century and preserve distinct apostolic traditions.

events.label: late 1st / early 2nd c.
events.title: Didache
events.summary: Early church-order text addressing Christian morals, Baptism, fasting, Eucharistic prayer, and community order.

events.label: c. AD 90s
events.title: Johannine writings and Revelation
events.summary: The Johannine corpus and Revelation are traditionally associated with the late apostolic period.

events.label: c. AD 96
events.title: 1 Clement to Corinth
events.summary: The Church of Rome writes to Corinth concerning order, ministry, and apostolic succession near the end of the first century.
events.source: 1 Clement / Open Apostolic Fathers / New Advent

events.label: c. AD 96
events.title: 1 Clement
events.summary: The Roman church’s letter known as 1 Clement is among the earliest surviving post-apostolic Christian writings.

events.label: late 1st–early 2nd c.
events.title: Didache
events.summary: The Didache preserves early Christian instruction on morality, Baptism, fasting, Eucharistic prayer, and church order.

events.label: c. AD 107
events.title: Ignatius of Antioch writes seven letters
events.summary: On the way to martyrdom, Ignatius witnesses to bishops, Eucharistic realism, unity, and the “Catholic Church.”
events.source: Ignatius / Open Apostolic Fathers / New Advent

events.label: c. AD 107
events.title: Ignatius of Antioch’s letters
events.summary: Ignatius writes to churches while being taken to martyrdom, witnessing to bishop-centered ecclesial life and Eucharistic faith.

events.label: c. AD 107
events.title: Ignatius, Smyrnaeans
events.summary: Primary-source witness useful for studying Eucharist, ecclesial unity, and the bishop.

events.label: early 2nd c.
events.title: Polycarp writes to the Philippians
events.summary: Polycarp’s letter preserves early Christian moral exhortation and links the apostolic and post-apostolic generations.

events.label: early 2nd c.
events.title: Polycarp to the Philippians
events.summary: Polycarp preserves an early pastoral witness closely connected with the apostolic generation.

events.label: c. AD 112
events.title: Pliny writes Trajan about Christians
events.summary: Pliny’s correspondence provides non-Christian evidence for Christian worship and legal pressure in Bithynia.

events.label: c. AD 155
events.title: Justin Martyr’s First Apology
events.summary: Justin describes Christian worship, Baptism, Sunday assembly, Scripture readings, and the Eucharist to a pagan audience.
events.source: Justin Martyr, First Apology / New Advent

events.label: c. AD 155–160
events.title: Martyrdom of Polycarp
events.summary: The Martyrdom of Polycarp is among the earliest detailed Christian martyr narratives.
events.source: Martyrdom of Polycarp / Open Apostolic Fathers

events.label: c. AD 155
events.title: Justin Martyr’s First Apology
events.summary: Justin describes Christian worship, Baptism, and Eucharistic practice in second-century Rome.

events.label: c. AD 155
events.title: Justin, First Apology 65–67
events.summary: Primary-source section commonly studied for Baptism, Eucharist, and Sunday Christian worship.

events.label: c. AD 180
events.title: Irenaeus writes Against Heresies
events.summary: Irenaeus appeals to apostolic succession, the rule of faith, Scripture, and Eucharistic doctrine against Gnosticism.

events.label: c. AD 180
events.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies
events.summary: Irenaeus argues from apostolic tradition, succession, Scripture, and the rule of faith against Gnostic systems.

events.label: c. AD 180
events.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III
events.summary: Primary-source material important for apostolic tradition, succession, Scripture, and public catholic teaching.

events.label: late 2nd c.
events.title: Muratorian Canon fragment
events.summary: The Muratorian fragment provides an early witness to a developing New Testament canon.

events.label: c. AD 197–220
events.title: Tertullian’s major Christian writings
events.summary: Tertullian provides early Latin Christian testimony on doctrine, discipline, Scripture, and sacramental practice.

events.label: early 3rd c.
events.title: Hippolytus and early Roman tradition
events.summary: Works associated with Hippolytus preserve important early theological and liturgical material, though attribution questions require care.

events.label: early–mid 3rd c.
events.title: Origen’s biblical scholarship
events.summary: Origen develops extensive biblical exegesis and textual scholarship, including the Hexapla.

events.label: AD 249–251
events.title: Decian persecution
events.summary: Imperial sacrifice requirements create a widespread crisis of persecution, apostasy, and reconciliation.

events.label: c. AD 250s
events.title: Cyprian on Church unity and reconciliation
events.summary: Cyprian of Carthage writes on episcopal unity, the lapsed, Baptism controversies, and ecclesial communion.

events.label: AD 257–260
events.title: Valerian persecution
events.summary: Imperial measures target Christian clergy and assemblies; Cyprian is martyred in 258.

events.label: AD 303–311
events.title: Great Persecution
events.summary: The Diocletianic persecution becomes the last and most severe empire-wide persecution before imperial toleration.

events.label: AD 311
events.title: Edict of toleration by Galerius
events.summary: Galerius ends the Great Persecution and permits Christians to exist and assemble under conditions.

events.label: AD 313
events.title: Edict of Milan / imperial toleration
events.summary: Constantine and Licinius establish broad religious toleration and restore confiscated Christian property.

events.label: AD 325
events.title: First Council of Nicaea
events.summary: The first ecumenical council addresses the Arian controversy and confesses the Son as consubstantial with the Father.

events.label: AD 325
events.title: First Council of Nicaea
events.summary: The council responds to Arianism and confesses the Son’s true divinity.

events.label: AD 381
events.title: First Council of Constantinople
events.summary: The Nicene faith is reaffirmed and the Church’s confession of the Holy Spirit is articulated against contemporary errors.

events.label: AD 381
events.title: First Council of Constantinople
events.summary: The council reaffirms Nicaea and clarifies teaching on the Holy Spirit, contributing to the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed.

events.label: AD 386
events.title: Conversion of Augustine
events.summary: Augustine’s conversion precedes his baptism and later immense influence on Western theology.

events.label: late 4th–early 5th c.
events.title: Jerome’s Latin biblical translation work
events.summary: Jerome’s translation and revision work becomes foundational to the Latin Vulgate tradition.

events.label: AD 410
events.title: Sack of Rome
events.summary: The Visigothic sack of Rome shocks the Roman world and provides the setting for Augustine’s City of God.

events.label: AD 431
events.title: Council of Ephesus
events.summary: The council defends the unity of Christ’s person and the title Theotokos, Mother of God.

events.label: AD 431
events.title: Council of Ephesus
events.summary: Ephesus addresses the Nestorian controversy and affirms Mary as Theotokos in defense of Christ’s unity.

events.label: AD 451
events.title: Council of Chalcedon
events.summary: Chalcedon confesses the one person of Christ in two natures, divine and human.

events.label: AD 451
events.title: Council of Chalcedon
events.summary: Chalcedon confesses Christ as one person in two natures and becomes a major Christological landmark.

events.label: after AD 451
events.title: Post-Chalcedonian separations
events.summary: Disputes surrounding Chalcedon contribute to enduring divisions among ancient Eastern Christian communities.

events.label: after AD 451
events.title: Post-Chalcedonian separations
events.summary: Disputes surrounding Chalcedon contribute to enduring separations between imperial Chalcedonian churches and Oriental Orthodox communities.

events.label: c. AD 529
events.title: Rule of St. Benedict
events.summary: Benedictine monasticism shapes Western prayer, learning, community life, and preservation of texts.
events.source: Rule of St. Benedict / New Advent

events.label: AD 553
events.title: Second Council of Constantinople
events.summary: The fifth ecumenical council addresses continuing Christological controversies after Chalcedon.

events.label: AD 590
events.title: Gregory the Great becomes pope
events.summary: Gregory’s pontificate influences pastoral theology, liturgy, missions, and medieval papal administration.

events.label: early 7th c.
events.title: Rise of Islam in Arabia
events.summary: Islam emerges in Arabia, creating a new religious and political force that soon transforms the eastern Mediterranean and Near East.

events.label: AD 630s–650s
events.title: Early Islamic conquests of Christian territories
events.summary: Arab Muslim armies take Syria, Palestine, Egypt, and other long-Christian regions from Byzantine and Persian rule.

events.label: AD 638
events.title: Jerusalem comes under Muslim rule
events.summary: Jerusalem passes from Byzantine to Muslim rule during the early Islamic conquests.

events.label: AD 680–681
events.title: Third Council of Constantinople
events.summary: The sixth ecumenical council rejects Monothelitism and affirms Christ’s two wills.

events.label: AD 787
events.title: Second Council of Nicaea
events.summary: The seventh ecumenical council addresses the iconoclast controversy and sacred images.

events.label: AD 787
events.title: Second Council of Nicaea
events.summary: The seventh ecumenical council defends the legitimate veneration of sacred images against iconoclasm.

events.label: AD 800
events.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
events.summary: The imperial coronation symbolizes a new relationship between the papacy and Western political order.

events.label: 9th c.
events.title: Mission of Cyril and Methodius
events.summary: The brothers evangelize Slavic peoples and promote liturgy and Scripture in Slavonic.

events.label: AD 910
events.title: Foundation of Cluny
events.summary: Cluniac monastic reform becomes a major force for renewal in medieval Western Christianity.

events.label: AD 1054 (long process)
events.title: East–West rupture conventionally dated to 1054
events.summary: The dissolution of communion between Eastern patriarchates and Rome developed through a long historical process, conventionally associated with 1054.

events.label: AD 1054
events.title: East–West rupture of 1054
events.summary: Mutual excommunications in 1054 become a symbolic landmark in the long estrangement between Rome and Constantinople.

events.label: AD 1071
events.title: Battle of Manzikert
events.summary: Byzantine defeat by Seljuk forces accelerates territorial losses in Anatolia and forms part of the background to later appeals for Western aid.

events.label: 11th c.
events.title: Gregorian Reform
events.summary: A broad medieval reform movement addressed clerical discipline, ecclesial governance, and freedom of the Church.

events.label: 11th c.
events.title: Gregorian Reform
events.summary: Reform efforts address clerical discipline, simony, investiture, and the freedom of ecclesiastical governance.

events.label: AD 1095
events.title: Council of Clermont and call for the First Crusade
events.summary: Urban II calls an armed pilgrimage after Byzantine appeals for assistance, amid concern for Eastern Christians and access to the Holy Land.

events.label: AD 1096–1099
events.title: First Crusade and capture of Jerusalem
events.summary: The First Crusade reaches Jerusalem and establishes Latin states in the eastern Mediterranean.

events.label: c. AD 1119
events.title: Military religious orders emerge
events.summary: Orders such as the Templars develop in the crusading context to protect pilgrims and support Latin states.

events.label: AD 1147–1149
events.title: Second Crusade
events.summary: A new crusade follows the fall of Edessa but fails to restore the lost territory.

events.label: AD 1187
events.title: Saladin captures Jerusalem
events.summary: Saladin defeats the crusader army at Hattin and retakes Jerusalem, prompting the Third Crusade.

events.label: AD 1189–1192
events.title: Third Crusade
events.summary: Western rulers campaign after Jerusalem’s loss; agreements preserve Christian pilgrimage access while Jerusalem remains under Muslim control.

events.label: AD 1204
events.title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
events.summary: The diversion and sack of Christian Constantinople gravely wounds East–West relations and departs from the crusade’s original purpose.

events.label: early 13th c.
events.title: Mendicant renewal
events.summary: Franciscan and Dominican movements become major forces of evangelical, pastoral, intellectual, and missionary renewal.

events.label: early 13th c.
events.title: Franciscan movement recognized
events.summary: The Franciscan movement renews evangelical poverty, preaching, mission, and service within the Church.

events.label: AD 1215
events.title: Fourth Lateran Council
events.summary: Lateran IV addresses doctrine, discipline, pastoral reform, and sacramental practice in medieval Christianity.

events.label: AD 1216
events.title: Dominican Order confirmed
events.summary: The Order of Preachers develops around preaching, study, and defense of the faith.

events.label: 13th c.
events.title: Thomas Aquinas and mature scholastic theology
events.summary: Aquinas integrates Scripture, Fathers, philosophy, and sacramental theology in a major synthesis of Catholic thought.

events.label: AD 1291
events.title: Fall of Acre
events.summary: The fall of Acre ends the principal Latin crusader foothold in the Holy Land.

events.label: AD 1309–1377
events.title: Avignon Papacy
events.summary: The papal residence at Avignon shapes late-medieval ecclesiastical politics and precedes the Western Schism.

events.title: Western Schism
events.summary: Competing papal claimants divide Western Christendom until the crisis is resolved at Constance.

events.label: AD 1378–1417
events.title: Western Schism
events.summary: Competing papal claimants divide Western Christendom until the Council of Constance resolves the crisis.

events.title: Council of Constance and end of Western Schism
events.summary: The council resolves the Western Schism; later conciliarist claims require careful distinction from Catholic teaching on primacy.

events.label: AD 1414–1418
events.title: Council of Constance
events.summary: Constance helps end the Western Schism and addresses major ecclesiastical controversies.

events.label: c. AD 1450s
events.title: Printing press transforms transmission of texts
events.summary: Movable-type printing dramatically expands access to Scripture, theology, liturgy, and polemical literature.

events.label: AD 1453
events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.summary: Ottoman conquest ends the Byzantine Empire and reshapes Christian-Muslim geopolitics.

events.label: AD 1492
events.title: Atlantic expansion and new missionary fields
events.summary: European Atlantic expansion opens vast new missionary contexts while also creating grave colonial abuses and moral controversies.

events.label: AD 1517
events.title: Luther and the Reformation crisis
events.summary: Luther’s protest becomes a catalyst for the Protestant Reformation and major doctrinal and ecclesial divisions in Western Christianity.

events.label: from 1517
events.title: Protestant Reformation
events.summary: Western reform controversies lead to multiple ecclesial communities separating from the Roman See.

events.label: AD 1531
events.title: Our Lady of Guadalupe tradition
events.summary: The Guadalupe tradition becomes central to Catholic evangelization and devotion in the Americas.

events.label: AD 1540
events.title: Society of Jesus approved
events.summary: The Jesuits become influential in education, missions, spiritual formation, and Catholic renewal.

events.label: AD 1542 onward
events.title: Francis Xavier’s Asian missions
events.summary: Francis Xavier undertakes major missionary work in India, Southeast Asia, and Japan.

events.title: Council of Trent and Catholic Reform
events.summary: Trent clarifies disputed doctrine and advances major Catholic disciplinary and pastoral reforms in response to the Reformation crisis.

events.label: AD 1545–1563
events.title: Council of Trent
events.summary: Trent clarifies Catholic doctrine, addresses reform, strengthens seminaries and catechesis, and responds to Reformation controversies.

events.label: AD 1566
events.title: Roman Catechism published
events.summary: The Catechism of the Council of Trent supports systematic pastoral teaching after the council.

events.label: AD 1571
events.title: Battle of Lepanto
events.summary: The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto, a major Mediterranean military event in Christian-Ottoman conflict.

events.label: AD 1582
events.title: Gregorian calendar reform
events.summary: Pope Gregory XIII promulgates calendar reform to correct accumulated drift in the Julian calendar.

events.label: AD 1633
events.title: Galileo trial
events.summary: The Galileo case becomes a lasting point of debate concerning biblical interpretation, scientific evidence, and Church authority.

events.label: AD 1648
events.title: Peace of Westphalia
events.summary: The settlement ends major European religious wars and reshapes the political order after the Reformation era.

events.label: AD 1789 onward
events.title: French Revolution and upheaval for the Church
events.summary: Revolutionary policies transform Church-state relations, suppress institutions, and provoke persecution and later reorganization.

events.label: AD 1854
events.title: Immaculate Conception defined
events.summary: Pius IX solemnly defines the Immaculate Conception of Mary.

events.label: AD 1858
events.title: Lourdes apparitions
events.summary: The Lourdes apparitions become a major modern Marian pilgrimage and devotional tradition recognized by the Church.

events.title: First Vatican Council
events.summary: Vatican I treats revelation, faith and reason, and papal primacy and infallibility before being interrupted in 1870.

events.label: AD 1870
events.title: End of the Papal States
events.summary: The capture of Rome ends the Papal States and creates the “Roman Question.”

events.label: AD 1891
events.title: Rerum Novarum
events.summary: Leo XIII’s social encyclical becomes a foundational modern Catholic social teaching document.

events.label: AD 1917
events.title: Fatima apparitions
events.summary: The Fatima apparitions become a major twentieth-century Marian devotion recognized by the Church.

events.label: AD 1929
events.title: Lateran Treaty
events.summary: The Lateran agreements resolve the Roman Question and establish Vatican City State.

events.label: AD 1939–1945
events.title: Second World War and the Church
events.summary: The global war, Holocaust, occupation, resistance, and persecution profoundly affect Catholic communities and later historical debate.

events.label: AD 1950
events.title: Assumption of Mary defined
events.summary: Pius XII solemnly defines the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

events.title: Second Vatican Council
events.summary: Vatican II addresses the Church, revelation, liturgy, ecumenism, mission, religious freedom, and the Church in the modern world.

events.label: AD 1965
events.title: Synod of Bishops established
events.summary: Paul VI establishes the Synod of Bishops as a permanent institution supporting episcopal collegial consultation.

events.title: 1983 Code of Canon Law
events.summary: The revised Latin Code implements legal renewal shaped by Vatican II.
events.source: Vatican Code of Canon Law introduction

events.label: AD 1992
events.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church promulgated
events.summary: John Paul II promulgates the Catechism as a reference text for Catholic doctrine and catechesis after Vatican II.

events.label: AD 1999
events.title: Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification
events.summary: Catholic and Lutheran representatives sign a major ecumenical declaration concerning justification.

events.label: AD 2001
events.title: Papal sorrow for the sack of Constantinople
events.summary: John Paul II expresses sorrow for the events of 1204, an important gesture in Catholic-Orthodox reconciliation.
